questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to stay at UBC for my exchange because I really wanted to experience Canada and the nature in the area surrounding Vancouver. UBC was also a good university with many interesting and relevant courses since I wanted to use my time on exchange to learn more about climate policy and forest conservation.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only negative part of the experience was the administrative and practical aspect of getting courses to work out.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I did not experience any problems in regards to this.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance was provided, but I found no need for it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a shared unit with 5 other girls. It was an apartment with my own room and shared kitchen/bathroom - and a balcony looking over the mountains and water:) It was my experience that a lot of exchange students lived in Walter Gage, which was the name of my residence, and at Fairview in the other end of campus. For law students and other students taking courses in the department of Arts Walter Gage is in the northern part of campus near the relevant building where the courses take place, so this is just a tip for a shorter commute.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You can buy the worlds most expensive meal plan but you are also free to just make food yourself. A tip is to always buy groceries off campus because this is a lot more affordable.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A tip is to always buy groceries off campus because this is a lot more affordable. The room you get on campus has no bedding so a way to save money is to buy this off other students leaving the unit prior to you arriving. You are given your future roommates contact information before arrival and sometimes people stay for two terms and therefore know people leaving who's things you can buy. Just a tip I wish I knew about beforehand.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was really not a good experience and it was completely due to KU's administrative process. UBC was very helpful and quick to answer but there was a lot of problems with KU and for months I was unsure of whether I could even go on exchange. Honestly one of the worst times of my life.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received an email from UBC where I could register for courses and rate them from 1-10. However, I did not end up getting any of my first choices but after writing back and forth with KU I made it work.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wrote a lot with the international office at UBC and at KU.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: European politics was not on the course list for the term I travelled to UBC because the professor was on research leave and this created a lot of problems during the months leading up to my arrival at UBC. Overall, I was happy where I ended up but I cannot stress enough how arduous the process leading up to my arrival was.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: UBC is way more flexible regarding courses than KU so this is by far where I would focus my energy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took one 200 level course and the rest were level 300 (third year).

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more hands on with more assignments, midterms and participation. I really enjoyed this way of learning and it allowed the final grade to be made up of different assignments instead of the final exam constituting 100pct. of the grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POLI_V 351 (001) Environmental Politics and Policy 
POLI_V 220A (001) Introduction to Political Systems Around the World - INTR COMP POLTCS 
GEOG_V 310 / ENST 310 Environment and Sustainability

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed the different courses on environmental politics and sustainability. The ENST 310 course was online but really well structured with a very supportive and educational professor. I would definitely recommend this course!

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had to buy new bedding for my room and getting a data plan in Canada is just generally really expensive compared to other countries. I ended up buying an esim but I would probably recommend also getting a Canadian phone number in case you need to rent a car and/or Airbnb.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries are expensive in Canada but compared to Copenhagen going out for dinner is more affordable. Public transport is cheap compared to Copenhagen because UBC has an arrangement with compass card where you get a deal as a student.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lot of sports events and homecoming games. UBC is massive and there is a club for everything - even a Scandinavia club if you get homesick.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend going to the homecoming games just for the experience. This was a lot of fun!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on weekend trips to the nearby islands, hike up the mountains, go whale watching, take the ferry and you might just get lucky and see whales here too, walk through their large forests near campus, walk along the shore surrounding UBC and so on and so on... the nature is beautiful and definitely worth prioritizing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not so bad. Everyone is super friendly and will always want to help both on and off campus. It was mostly the different currency and tipping culture I needed to settle into.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is really helpful to choose shared housing where you live with others. This was a very positive experience for me. And it is really great to just ask people around you if they want toy join you for a weekend trip. Everyone is there to have fun and see Vancouver and being the one to take initiative allows you to meet new people. The varsity outdoor club also arranges plenty of hikes so be sure to sign up!:)

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: For the most part it was an easy culture to fit into.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Peoples outgoing and friendly way of being was a big part of how quickly I settled in. Canadians are generally very friendly and understanding the language breaks down a lot of barriers when moving to a new part of the world.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to get student housing on campus - this was a huge plus for me (and honestly a good price compared to options off campus). Bring good hiking boots! And honestly communicate with UCPH over email so you have the correspondence in print so you can refer back to earlier answers and agreements at a later time since the process of getting admitted to courses is pretty long and it can be really constructive to have your agreements written down officially since you are communicating with multiple universities and offices at the same time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: When you make it through the process of getting admitted to courses the exchange experience is amazing and completely worth it!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Seeing the nature and getting to live in a part of the world I have wanted to see all my life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having a long time of mingling and getting to know other people without having my old social group from home around. Although this was also a big plus and it allowed me to meet some of the nicest people.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
